title: The angels
hook: created from light, obeying, never tiring

segments.voice: Yesterday, Allah, the One, four verses that equal a third, and your line: one. When your attention split into pieces, did you find the next single thing? Day one thousand two hundred thirty-five.

Watch the end of any Muslim prayer. The person sitting on the floor turns the head to the right and says peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah. Then to the left, the same words. If they're praying in a row, there's a person on each side, so the greeting lands somewhere. But some scholars say it's meant for more than the neighbors. They say it's also for the angels, the ones the Qur'an describes as noble recorders, keeping watch over every person. So a small turn of the head at the close of prayer is a hello to the second article of faith.
screen: `RIGHT, THEN LEFT.` → `PEACE BE UPON YOU.` → `TO WHOM?`

segments.voice: Start with what they're made of. A hadith in Sahih Muslim says the angels were created from light, the jinn from smokeless fire, and Adam from what you have been told: the earth. Three kinds of creature, three materials. Next, what they do. The Qur'an describes angels who carry out what they're commanded and do not disobey, and others who glorify Allah night and day without tiring. Some are known by name and task: Jibril who brought the revelation, Mika'il, and the angel of death. Others record, others guard. Then, a surprise. Obedient doesn't mean silent. In the second surah, Allah tells the angels, in Pickthall's translation, "Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth." And the angels ask a question. Will you put there someone who will do harm and shed blood, when we praise you? Allah answers that He knows what they don't. Then Adam is taught the names of things, and the angels admit they know only what they've been taught. The beings of light ask, and then they learn. Last, why believe in them at all. For Muslims, angels are part of how the unseen world works. Revelation came through one. Deeds are written by others. In this belief, no deed goes unwitnessed. That is held not as a mood but as an article of faith, the second of the six.
screen: `LIGHT, FIRE, EARTH.` · `THEY OBEY AND DON'T TIRE.` · `THE ANGELS ASKED A QUESTION.` · then, large: `NO DEED UNWITNESSED.`

segments.voice: The practice: greet the angels, the way the end of the prayer does. Sit, and settle. Breathe a few times. Then turn your head gently to the right, and say, aloud or inside, peace be upon you. Turn to the left, and say it again. Then face forward and stay there. If you pray, this is the greeting you already know. If you don't, take it as a greeting to whatever company you keep: the people near you, and whatever is unseen. Then just sit, facing forward. The bell holds the time.
The angels. Mala'ikah in Arabic: created from light, obeying their Lord, glorifying Him without tiring. The second article of faith. Today's word.

Your line: made of light. Today, when you walk into a room, say peace in your head to everyone there, seen and unseen. Tomorrow, the third article: the books. Day one thousand two hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: Muslims end each prayer by turning the head right and left with the words peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah; belief in angels, including Jibril and the recording angels, is the second article of faith.

fork.setup: you are one of the angels. Allah says, I am about to place a viceroy in the earth. what do you do?
options: ask: will you put there someone who will do harm and shed blood?
fork.reveal: in Surah al-Baqarah the angels ask exactly that. Allah answers that He knows what they don't, and then Adam is taught the names.

original.note: Arabic: angels; one angel is malak.

trapdoor: what you thought: angels are winged babies on greeting cards.
what it means: in Islam, angels are beings of light who carry out Allah's commands: bringing revelation, recording deeds, guarding.
what a scholar hears: the hadith of the three materials, the angels' question in Surah al-Baqarah, and the discussion of whom the closing salam of prayer addresses.
